people.name: George Washington
people.blurb: Led the Revolution, then handed power back instead of becoming king. Set the bar so high every president since has been quietly disappointing the cherry tree.

people.name: Thomas Jefferson
people.blurb: Wrote the Declaration of Independence at 33. Also invented a swivel chair so he could avoid eye contact more efficiently.

people.name: Benjamin Franklin
people.blurb: Tamed lightning, invented bifocals, and basically lobbied Europe into funding America. The original founding influencer.

people.name: John Adams
people.blurb: Second president and the guy who argued everyone else into independence. Loud, stubborn, usually right.

people.name: Alexander Hamilton
people.blurb: Built the financial system from scratch and got a hit musical out of it. Lost the duel, won the soundtrack.

people.name: James Madison
people.blurb: Father of the Constitution and the Bill of Rights. Proof you don't need to be the tallest guy in the room to run it.

people.name: John Hancock
people.blurb: Signed his name so big the King could read it without glasses. The original power move.

people.name: Patrick Henry
people.blurb: 'Give me liberty or give me death.' Delivered the ultimate ultimatum and somehow got the liberty.

people.name: Paul Revere
people.blurb: Midnight rider who warned the colonists the British were coming. America's first emergency alert system.

people.name: Thomas Paine
people.blurb: Wrote 'Common Sense' and lit the fuse on the whole revolution with a pamphlet. The power of good copywriting.

people.name: Abraham Lincoln
people.blurb: Held the Union together and ended slavery, all in a stovepipe hat. Tallest president, biggest legacy.

people.name: Ulysses S Grant
people.blurb: Won the Civil War for the Union, then became president. Smoked cigars like it was cardio.

people.name: Andrew Jackson
people.blurb: Tough-as-nails populist who survived multiple duels. The angriest face on your money.

people.name: Theodore Roosevelt
people.blurb: Cowboy, war hero, trust-buster, and the reason teddy bears exist. Spoke softly, carried a very big stick.

people.name: Frederick Douglass
people.blurb: Escaped slavery and became the most powerful voice for abolition in America. Out-argued anyone who tried him.

people.name: Franklin D Roosevelt
people.blurb: Led America through the Depression and most of WWII from a wheelchair. Four terms, zero quit.

people.name: Dwight D Eisenhower
people.blurb: Ran D-Day, then ran the country, then built the highways you're stuck in traffic on.

people.name: John F Kennedy
people.blurb: Charisma in a suit. Dodged nuclear war, aimed America at the moon.

people.name: Ronald Reagan
people.blurb: Actor turned president who told Gorbachev to tear down a wall. The Great Communicator.

people.name: George H W Bush
people.blurb: WWII pilot, CIA chief, president. Skydived on his 90th birthday for fun.

people.name: George W Bush
people.blurb: 43rd president. Now spends his retirement painting portraits, which nobody saw coming.

people.name: John Mcenroe
people.blurb: Tennis genius and tantrum legend. 'You cannot be serious!' He was.

people.name: Chipper Jones
people.blurb: Braves third-base legend and Hall of Famer. A switch-hitting nightmare for the Mets.

people.name: Donald Trump
people.blurb: 45th and 47th president, reality TV star, and the most argued-about hair in America.

people.name: Richard Nixon
people.blurb: Opened China, then closed his own presidency. 'I am not a crook' did not age well.

people.name: Harry Truman
people.blurb: Made the toughest call of the 20th century. 'The buck stops here' — and it did.

people.name: Colin Powell
people.blurb: Four-star general and Secretary of State. The steady hand in every crisis room.

people.name: George S Patton
people.blurb: WWII general who treated war like a contact sport. Ivory-handled pistols, zero chill.

people.name: Douglas Macarthur
people.blurb: 'I shall return' — and he did. Corncob pipe, mirrored shades, maximum drama.

people.name: Chief Nokahoma
people.blurb: The old Atlanta Braves mascot. A piece of franchise history with a feathered headdress and a tomahawk chop.

people.name: Chris Kyle
people.blurb: The most lethal sniper in U.S. history and the man behind 'American Sniper.'

people.name: Pat Tillman
people.blurb: Walked away from an NFL contract to become an Army Ranger. The definition of putting country first.

people.name: Michael Vick
people.blurb: Electric dual-threat quarterback who could outrun a defense and a highlight reel. Pictured next to a very good boy.

people.name: A Pit Bull Dog
people.blurb: America's most loyal (and most misunderstood) good boy. Placed here for… reasons. Look to the left.

people.name: Sequoyah
people.blurb: The Cherokee genius who single-handedly invented a written language. One man, an entire alphabet.

people.name: Geronimo
people.blurb: Legendary Apache warrior and leader. So fearless his name became what you yell jumping out of a plane.

people.name: Alan Jackson
people.blurb: Country traditionalist with a stack of No. 1 hits and a cowboy hat that never came off.

people.name: Chuck Yeager
people.blurb: First man to break the sound barrier. Did it with two broken ribs and didn't mention it.

people.name: Charlie Kirk
people.blurb: Conservative commentator and campus debate fixture. Loves a microphone.

people.name: Marcus Luttrell
people.blurb: Navy SEAL and 'Lone Survivor.' Walked off a mountain that should've ended him.

people.name: Desmond Doss
people.blurb: WWII medic who saved 75 men without ever firing a shot. 'Hacksaw Ridge' hero.

people.name: Johnny Knoxville
people.blurb: Jackass ringleader who turned getting hurt into an art form. Hi, I'm Johnny Knoxville.

people.name: Jocko Willink
people.blurb: SEAL commander turned discipline guru. Wakes up at 4:30am to make you feel lazy.

people.name: Herschel Walker
people.blurb: Heisman winner, NFL bruiser, and a man who once did 1,000 push-ups a day.

people.name: Davy Crockett
people.blurb: King of the Wild Frontier who died at the Alamo. The coonskin cap was a choice and he committed.

people.name: Neil Armstrong
people.blurb: First human to walk on the moon. One small step, one giant flex for mankind.

people.name: Buzz Aldrin
people.blurb: Second man on the moon and the first to punch a guy who said it was fake. Legend.

people.name: John Glenn
people.blurb: First American to orbit Earth, then went back to space at 77 just to show off.

people.name: Johnny Manziel
people.blurb: Johnny Football. Heisman magic, money fingers, and the wildest college highlight reel.

people.name: Sally Ride
people.blurb: First American woman in space and an absolute trailblazer in zero gravity.

people.name: Where S Waldo
people.blurb: Striped shirt, bobble hat, impossible to find. Fitting that he's hidden in here somewhere too.

people.name: Oj Simpson
people.blurb: Hall of Fame running back turned the most-watched trial in history. The Juice.

people.name: Adam Sandler
people.blurb: From SNL to Sandman empire. Hoodie-and-shorts billionaire who just wants to make you laugh.

people.name: Thomas Edison
people.blurb: Held over 1,000 patents including the light bulb. The original 'I'll sleep when I'm dead.'

people.name: Nikola Tesla
people.blurb: Genius who basically invented the modern electrical grid and died broke. The patron saint of being right too early.

people.name: Henry Ford
people.blurb: Put America on wheels with the assembly line. Any color you want, as long as it's black.

people.name: Wright Brothers
people.blurb: Two bike mechanics who taught humanity to fly. Twelve seconds that changed everything.

people.name: Alexander Graham Bell
people.blurb: Invented the telephone, accidentally created the awkward 'you hang up first' call.

people.name: Steve Jobs
people.blurb: Put a thousand songs, then the whole internet, in your pocket. Turtleneck included.

people.name: Bill Gates
people.blurb: Built Microsoft, then pivoted to saving the world from disease. Richest nerd alive for a while.

people.name: Elon Musk
people.blurb: Rockets, electric cars, and the world's most chaotic social media feed. Never boring.

people.name: Jeff Bezos
people.blurb: Started in a garage selling books, now owns the box on your porch.

people.name: Warren Buffett
people.blurb: The Oracle of Omaha. Worth billions, still eats McDonald's and drinks Cherry Coke.

people.name: Sam Walton
people.blurb: Built Walmart into a retail empire and still drove an old pickup. Frugal to the end.

people.name: Buddy Holly
people.blurb: Glasses, hiccup vocals, and the blueprint for rock. Gone way too soon.

people.name: A Crips Gang Member
people.blurb: A nod to West Coast street history and hip-hop legend. (You'll have to guess the colors — it's black and white.)

people.name: John D Rockefeller
people.blurb: First American billionaire. Owned oil before oil was cool.

people.name: A Bloods Gang Member
people.blurb: The other side of that same coin. Immortalized in countless lyrics and films.

people.name: Jeff Foxworthy
people.blurb: 'You might be a redneck if…' Built an empire on knowing his audience.

people.name: Howard Hughes
people.blurb: Aviator, filmmaker, billionaire eccentric. Lived like a movie, ended like a mystery.

people.name: Ray Kroc
people.blurb: Turned a burger stand into McDonald's. Sold a billion fries and a dream.

people.name: Lindsey Vonn
people.blurb: One of the greatest ski racers ever. Bombed down mountains faster than most people drive.

people.name: Mark Zuckerberg
people.blurb: Built Facebook in a dorm room and rewired how the planet argues with relatives.

people.name: Hugh Hefner
people.blurb: Built a magazine empire in silk pajamas. Worked from home before it was cool.

people.name: Colonel Harland Sanders
people.blurb: Failed at everything until 65, then founded KFC. Eleven herbs, infinite redemption.

people.name: Martin Luther King Jr
people.blurb: Led the Civil Rights Movement with a dream and changed America forever.

people.name: Rosa Parks
people.blurb: Refused to give up her bus seat and moved a nation by sitting still.

people.name: Malcolm X
people.blurb: Fiery, fearless voice for Black empowerment. By any means necessary.

people.name: Harriet Tubman
people.blurb: Escaped slavery, then went back again and again to free others. The conductor of the Underground Railroad.

people.name: Susan B Anthony
people.blurb: Fought for women's right to vote and got arrested for trying. Now she's on a coin.

people.name: Monica Lewinsky
people.blurb: Defined a chapter of '90s history and turned it into anti-bullying advocacy. Conveniently next to a familiar face.

people.name: Bill Clinton
people.blurb: Saxophone-playing president of the booming '90s. Conveniently standing right next to someone on this shirt.

people.name: John Lewis
people.blurb: Civil rights icon who spent a lifetime making 'good trouble.'

people.name: Jesse James
people.blurb: America's most famous outlaw. Robbed trains, dodged the law, became a legend.

people.name: Billy The Kid
people.blurb: Wild West gunslinger who died at 21 with a body count and a legend bigger than both.

people.name: Wyatt Earp
people.blurb: Lawman of the O.K. Corral. The mustache alone kept the peace.

people.name: Wild Bill Hickok
people.blurb: Gunfighter and gambler who died holding aces and eights — the 'dead man's hand.'

people.name: Doc Holliday
people.blurb: Tubercular dentist turned deadliest gunslinger in the West. Coughing, shooting, legendary.

people.name: Al Capone
people.blurb: Chicago's most notorious gangster. Brought down not by murder, but by taxes.

people.name: John Dillinger
people.blurb: Depression-era bank robber and Public Enemy No. 1. Charm and a getaway car.

people.name: Bonnie And Clyde
people.blurb: The crime spree couple who turned robbery into romance and went out in a blaze.

people.name: Annie Oakley
people.blurb: Sharpshooter who could split a card edge-on. 'Little Sure Shot' never missed.

people.name: Buffalo Bill Cody
people.blurb: Turned the Wild West into a traveling show. The original showman of the frontier.

people.name: Michael Jordan
people.blurb: The greatest to ever lace up. Six rings, one tongue out, infinite highlight reels.

people.name: David Lee Roth
people.blurb: Van Halen's spandex-clad ringmaster. Did the splits, hit the highs, lived loud.

people.name: Kobe Bryant
people.blurb: Mamba Mentality incarnate. Five rings and a work ethic that scared people.

people.name: Magic Johnson
people.blurb: Point guard in a power forward's body. Made winning look like a smile.

people.name: Larry Bird
people.blurb: Trash-talked you, then drained the three. The Hick from French Lick.

people.name: Shaquille O Neal
people.blurb: Most dominant big man ever and the only Hall of Famer who could shatter a backboard and a one-liner.

people.name: Kareem Abdul Jabbar
people.blurb: The skyhook was literally unguardable. All-time leading scorer for decades.

people.name: Stephen Curry
people.blurb: Broke basketball by making the three-pointer a layup. The Baby-Faced Assassin.

people.name: Wilt Chamberlain
people.blurb: Scored 100 points in a single game. Nobody's touching that one.

people.name: Scottie Scheffler
people.blurb: World No. 1 golfer who wins majors with the calmest demeanor in sports.

people.name: Allen Iverson
people.blurb: Pound-for-pound the toughest guy in the league. 'We talkin' bout practice?'

people.name: Charles Barkley
people.blurb: Round Mound of Rebound turned the funniest man on TV. Says the quiet part loud.

people.name: Dennis Rodman
people.blurb: Rebounding machine, walking tie-dye, and the NBA's most unpredictable diplomat.

people.name: Caitlyn Jenner
people.blurb: Olympic decathlon gold medalist and one of the most famous figures of the 2010s.

people.name: Tom Brady
people.blurb: Seven Super Bowl rings. The GOAT who refused to retire on time.

people.name: Jerry Rice
people.blurb: Greatest wide receiver ever. Ran routes until defenders filed complaints.

people.name: Joe Montana
people.blurb: Joe Cool. Four Super Bowls, ice in his veins, comeback king.

people.name: Walter Payton
people.blurb: 'Sweetness' ran like a freight train with ballet feet.

people.name: Jim Brown
people.blurb: Maybe the greatest running back ever, and he walked away on top.

people.name: Lawrence Taylor
people.blurb: Changed how defense is played by terrorizing quarterbacks. A force of nature.

people.name: Peyton Manning
people.blurb: Cerebral assassin at the line. 'Omaha!' and a thousand audibles.

people.name: Brett Favre
people.blurb: Gunslinger who played like a kid in the backyard. Threw it deep, lived loud.

people.name: Deion Sanders
people.blurb: 'Prime Time.' Two sports, all flash, never got his jersey dirty.

people.name: Barry Sanders
people.blurb: Made grown men miss in phone booths. The most electric runs ever.

people.name: Bruce Jenner
people.blurb: '70s Wheaties-box Olympic hero. Won decathlon gold and the title 'World's Greatest Athlete.'

people.name: John Madden
people.blurb: Coach, broadcaster, and the name on the game you've played for 30 years. Boom!

people.name: Vince Lombardi
people.blurb: The trophy is named after him for a reason. 'Winning isn't everything — it's the only thing.'

people.name: The Fat Man Atomic Bomb
people.blurb: 'Fat Man' — the bomb dropped on Nagasaki that ended WWII. History's heaviest paperweight.

people.name: Babe Ruth
people.blurb: The Sultan of Swat. Called his shot, ate hot dogs, built Yankee Stadium with home runs.

people.name: Jackie Robinson
people.blurb: Broke baseball's color barrier and changed America. Courage in cleats.

people.name: Lou Gehrig
people.blurb: The Iron Horse. 'Today I consider myself the luckiest man on the face of the earth.'

people.name: Hank Aaron
people.blurb: Broke the home run record under threats and pressure, with pure class.

people.name: Willie Mays
people.blurb: 'The Catch' and the five-tool blueprint. The Say Hey Kid did it all.

people.name: Mickey Mantle
people.blurb: Switch-hitting Yankee legend. Tape-measure homers and tape-measure stories.

people.name: Ted Williams
people.blurb: Last man to hit .400. Possibly the greatest pure hitter ever.

people.name: Joe Dimaggio
people.blurb: 56-game hit streak that'll never be broken. Smooth as silk in center.

people.name: Ken Griffey Jr
people.blurb: The Kid. Sweetest swing in baseball and a backwards cap to match.

people.name: Derek Jeter
people.blurb: Mr. November. Captain Clutch made the Yankees the Yankees.

people.name: Nolan Ryan
people.blurb: Seven no-hitters and a fastball that whistled. Also fought a guy 20 years younger and won.

people.name: Cal Ripken Jr
people.blurb: Played 2,632 straight games. Iron Man never called in sick. Ever.

people.name: Pete Rose
people.blurb: 'Charlie Hustle' — most hits in history, banned for betting. Complicated legend.

people.name: Barry Bonds
people.blurb: Home run king. Asterisk optional, raw talent undeniable.

people.name: Roberto Clemente
people.blurb: Hall of Famer and humanitarian who died delivering aid. A true hero.

people.name: John Rocker
people.blurb: Braves flamethrower famous for a 100-mph fastball and a zero-mph filter.

people.name: Muhammad Ali
people.blurb: The Greatest. Floated, stung, and talked more trash than anyone before or since.

people.name: Mike Tyson
people.blurb: Baddest man on the planet. Youngest heavyweight champ ever, scariest 90 seconds in sports.

people.name: Eric Cartman
people.blurb: South Park's tiny tyrant. 'Respect my authoritah!' Pure animated chaos.

people.name: Waylon Jennings
people.blurb: Outlaw country pioneer and the voice of 'The Dukes of Hazzard.'

people.name: Rosie The Riveter
people.blurb: 'We Can Do It!' The flexing symbol of every woman who built America during WWII.

people.name: George Foreman
people.blurb: Knocked people out, then sold them grills. The friendliest puncher alive.

people.name: Chuck Liddell
people.blurb: The Iceman who put the UFC on the map with a mohawk and a knockout.

people.name: Jon Jones
people.blurb: Maybe the greatest MMA fighter ever. Reach like a pterodactyl.

people.name: Tiger Woods
people.blurb: Changed golf forever. The Sunday red shirt still gives people chills.

people.name: Jack Nicklaus
people.blurb: The Golden Bear. 18 majors, the record everyone's chasing.

people.name: Arnold Palmer
people.blurb: Made golf cool and got a drink named after him. 'The King.'

people.name: John Daly
people.blurb: Golf's working-class wild man. Grip it, rip it, light a cigarette, repeat.

people.name: Dale Earnhardt
people.blurb: The Intimidator. Drove the 3 car like it owed him money.

people.name: Richard Petty
people.blurb: The King of NASCAR. 200 wins, a cowboy hat, and a feathered band.

people.name: Jeff Gordon
people.blurb: Brought a new generation to NASCAR and won everywhere. Rainbow warrior.

people.name: Serena Williams
people.blurb: The greatest tennis player of all time. 23 Slams and a serve like a cannon.

people.name: Michael Phelps
people.blurb: 23 Olympic golds. The most decorated Olympian ever, basically half-fish.

people.name: Lance Armstrong
people.blurb: Seven Tour wins, then the asterisk heard 'round the world. Pedaled hard, fell harder.

people.name: Tony Hawk
people.blurb: Landed the 900 and became skateboarding itself. Still gets ID'd as 'that Tony Hawk guy.'

people.name: Evel Knievel
people.blurb: Jumped buses, canyons, and common sense. Broke 433 bones and zero promises to entertain.

people.name: Julius Erving
people.blurb: Dr. J brought style and gravity-defying dunks to the game. Pure cool.

people.name: Bo Jackson
people.blurb: Two-sport superhuman. Broke bats over his head and the laws of physics.

people.name: Hulk Hogan
people.blurb: Brother, he told millions of Hulkamaniacs to train, say their prayers, and eat their vitamins. 24-inch pythons.

people.name: Ric Flair
people.blurb: WOOOO! 16-time champ, custom robes, and the limousine-ridin', jet-flyin' lifestyle to match.

people.name: Macho Man Randy Savage
people.blurb: 'Oooh yeah!' Snapped into a generation's memory. Sunglasses indoors, always.

people.name: Andre The Giant
people.blurb: 7-foot-4 gentle giant who could reportedly drink 100 beers. The Eighth Wonder of the World.

people.name: Stone Cold Steve Austin
people.blurb: 'And that's the bottom line, 'cause Stone Cold said so.' Beer, boots, and broken bosses.

people.name: The Rock
people.blurb: Can you smell what The Rock is cookin'? Went from the ring to the biggest star in Hollywood.

people.name: The Undertaker
people.blurb: 21-0 at WrestleMania. The Deadman buried opponents for three decades.

people.name: Floyd Mayweather
people.blurb: 50-0, never lost, 'Money' made defense an art form and a flex.

people.name: Elvis Presley
people.blurb: The King of Rock and Roll. Hips that scandalized a nation, a voice that conquered it.

people.name: Johnny Cash
people.blurb: The Man in Black. Walked the line, played Folsom, growled his way into legend.

people.name: Bob Dylan
people.blurb: Voice of a generation and a Nobel Prize winner. Nobody fully understands him, including him.

people.name: Jimi Hendrix
people.blurb: Played guitar with his teeth and set it on fire. Rewired what the instrument could do.

people.name: Bruce Springsteen
people.blurb: The Boss. Three-hour shows and working-class anthems. Born to run, built to last.

people.name: Prince
people.blurb: Genius in heels. Played every instrument and out-cooled everyone in the room.

people.name: Michael Jackson
people.blurb: The King of Pop. Moonwalked into history. 'Thriller' still owns October.

people.name: Madonna
people.blurb: Reinvented herself a dozen times and pop music with her. The Queen of reinvention.

people.name: Stevie Wonder
people.blurb: Blind since infancy, sees music better than anyone. A catalog of pure joy.

people.name: Willie Nelson
people.blurb: Outlaw country's beloved grandpa. Braids, a guitar named Trigger, and zero regrets.

people.name: Dolly Parton
people.blurb: Country royalty with a heart as big as the hair. Wrote two classics in one day.

people.name: Janis Joplin
people.blurb: Raw, electric blues voice of the '60s. Burned bright and fast.

people.name: Kurt Cobain
people.blurb: Reluctant voice of Gen X. Nirvana made flannel a uniform and angst an anthem.

people.name: Tom Petty
people.blurb: Heartland rock's everyman. 'I Won't Back Down' is basically a national mood.

people.name: Frank Sinatra
people.blurb: Ol' Blue Eyes. Did it his way and made the whole Rat Pack era look effortless.

people.name: Ray Charles
people.blurb: Genius who fused gospel, blues, and soul. Saw music nobody else could.

people.name: Aretha Franklin
people.blurb: The Queen of Soul. R-E-S-P-E-C-T, spelled out once and for all.

people.name: Whitney Houston
people.blurb: The Voice. Hit notes that physics is still investigating.

people.name: Popeye
people.blurb: Spinach-powered sailor with anchor tattoos and zero chill. 'I yam what I yam.'

people.name: Chuck Berry
people.blurb: Father of rock and roll and the duck walk. Every riff owes him rent.

people.name: Hank Williams
people.blurb: The original tortured country soul. Wrote the saddest songs in the catalog.

people.name: Joe Biden
people.blurb: 46th president. Aviators, ice cream, and — wait, why is he upside down? Look closer.

people.name: Tina Turner
people.blurb: Simply the best. Survived everything and out-danced everyone half her age.

people.name: Jim Morrison
people.blurb: The Lizard King. Poet, provocateur, and the brooding face of the '60s.

people.name: You Tommy
people.blurb: Wait… who's that? Doesn't ring a bell. Probably nobody. Definitely not the guy who made this shirt. Move along.

people.name: Weird Al Yankovic
people.blurb: Turned parody into an art form and outlasted half the artists he spoofed. Accordion forever.

people.name: Sugar Ray Robinson
people.blurb: Pound-for-pound the best ever. The standard every fighter is measured against.

people.name: The Notorious B I G
people.blurb: Biggie. Brooklyn's finest, smoothest flow in the game. King of New York.

people.name: Eminem
people.blurb: Fastest pen in rap. Turned trailer-park rage into the best-selling artist of a decade.

people.name: Snoop Dogg
people.blurb: From gangsta rap legend to America's favorite uncle. Smooth as ever, fo' shizzle.

people.name: Dr Dre
people.blurb: Super-producer who built empires and headphones. The beat behind the West Coast.

people.name: Rocky Marciano
people.blurb: 49-0, the only undefeated heavyweight champ to retire and stay retired.

people.name: Kanye West
people.blurb: Genius producer, genuine wildcard. Makes headlines and classics in equal measure.

people.name: Ice Cube
people.blurb: N.W.A's fiercest pen turned Hollywood mogul. Went from 'Today Was a Good Day' to family comedies.

people.name: 50 Cent
people.blurb: Survived nine shots, then dominated rap and TV. The ultimate comeback story.

people.name: Nas
people.blurb: 'Illmatic' is basically the rap dictionary. Queensbridge's poet laureate.

people.name: Lil Wayne
people.blurb: Self-proclaimed best rapper alive and a generational influence. Skateboarding optional.

people.name: Flavor Flav
people.blurb: Public Enemy's hype man with the giant clock necklace. Always knows what time it is.

people.name: Marilyn Monroe
people.blurb: The ultimate Hollywood icon. A subway grate and a white dress did the rest.

people.name: John Wayne
people.blurb: The Duke. Western royalty who walked tall and talked slow.

people.name: James Dean
people.blurb: Rebel without a cause and the eternal symbol of cool. Forever young.

people.name: Marlon Brando
people.blurb: Changed acting forever. 'I coulda been a contender' — he was the contender.

people.name: Clint Eastwood
people.blurb: Squint, poncho, cigarillo. Made everyone's day, then directed the movie too.

people.name: Robert De Niro
people.blurb: 'You talkin' to me?' The greatest of his generation, gangster or grandpa.

people.name: Al Pacino
people.blurb: From Michael Corleone to 'HOO-AH!' Intensity with an exclamation point.

people.name: Jack Nicholson
people.blurb: Those eyebrows, that grin. 'Heeere's Johnny!' and three Oscars.

people.name: Bill Russell
people.blurb: Eleven championships in thirteen seasons. The ultimate winner.

people.name: Carl Lewis
people.blurb: Nine Olympic golds in track. Flew down the runway and the track.

people.name: Samuel L Jackson
people.blurb: The coolest man in any room, in every movie ever made apparently. Say it again.

people.name: Bobby Knight
people.blurb: Hall of Fame coach with a Hall of Fame temper. Won big, threw chairs bigger.

people.name: Sylvester Stallone
people.blurb: Rocky and Rambo in one guy. Wrote himself into legend, literally.

people.name: Morgan Freeman
people.blurb: The voice of God, narrator of everything, calmest man in cinema.

people.name: Norman Schwarzkopf
people.blurb: 'Stormin' Norman' ran the Gulf War like a man with a deadline.

people.name: Alan Shepard
people.blurb: First American in space — and the only man to hit a golf ball on the moon.

people.name: Danny Devito
people.blurb: Pint-sized powerhouse. Equal parts beloved and gremlin, in the best way.

people.name: Steve Buscemi
people.blurb: Character-actor royalty with the most distinctive face in cinema. 'How do you do, fellow kids?'

people.name: Keanu Reeves
people.blurb: Action legend and the internet's favorite nice guy. Whoa.

people.name: Charlie Chaplin
people.blurb: The Little Tramp. Made the whole world laugh without saying a word.

people.name: Humphrey Bogart
people.blurb: 'Here's looking at you, kid.' The blueprint for the tough, tender leading man.

people.name: Bette Davis
people.blurb: Old Hollywood's fiercest. 'Fasten your seatbelts, it's going to be a bumpy night.'

people.name: Robin Williams
people.blurb: A comet of comedy and heart. Made everyone laugh, then cry. Genie forever.

people.name: Richard Pryor
people.blurb: The most influential stand-up ever. Raw, fearless, hilarious.

people.name: George Carlin
people.blurb: Comedy's philosopher king. Seven words and a lifetime of truth-telling.

people.name: Eddie Murphy
people.blurb: SNL legend turned box-office king. The laugh alone is worth the ticket.

people.name: Chris Farley
people.blurb: Tasmanian devil of comedy. Lived in a van down by the river, rent-free in our hearts.

people.name: Jim Lovell
people.blurb: Commander of Apollo 13. 'Houston, we have a problem' — and he solved it.

people.name: J P Morgan
people.blurb: Banker so powerful he personally bailed out the U.S. government. Twice.

people.name: Will Ferrell
people.blurb: Loud, ridiculous, perfect. Stayed classy and never broke character.

people.name: Dave Chappelle
people.blurb: Stand-up GOAT contender. Walked away from millions, came back even bigger. (Pictured: a certain crusty-lipped character.)

people.name: Cornelius Vanderbilt
people.blurb: Railroad and shipping tycoon. The 'Commodore' who basically owned 19th-century transportation.

people.name: Mr T
people.blurb: Gold chains, mohawk, and zero patience for fools. 'I pity the fool.'

people.name: Pauly Shore
people.blurb: The Weasel. '90s slacker comedy in human form. Buuuuddy.

people.name: Ronald Mcdonald
people.blurb: Fast food's favorite clown. Sold more burgers than anyone in a red wig should be allowed to.

people.name: Chuck E Cheese
people.blurb: Where a kid can be a kid — and a mouse can run an arcade empire. Charles Entertainment Cheese, esquire.

people.name: Kenny Powers
people.blurb: Mullet, mustache, and a fastball-sized ego. America's most delusional closer.

people.name: Paris Hilton
people.blurb: The original 2000s 'famous for being famous.' That's hot.

people.name: Guy Fieri
people.blurb: Mayor of Flavortown. Spiky hair, flame shirts, and a one-way ticket to Donkey Sauce.

people.name: David Hasselhoff
people.blurb: Baywatch slow-mo and a singing career Germany inexplicably loved. The Hoff abides.

people.name: Joey Chestnut
people.blurb: Competitive eating GOAT. Inhaled 76 hot dogs in 10 minutes. A true American stomach.

people.name: Larry The Cable Guy
people.blurb: 'Git-R-Done!' Flannel, catchphrase, and blue-collar comedy gold.

people.name: Billy Mays
people.blurb: The loudest pitchman in TV history. OxiClean's hype man, RIP. BUT WAIT, THERE'S MORE.

people.name: Hunter S Thompson
people.blurb: Gonzo journalism's deranged genius. We can't stop here, this is bat country.

people.name: Uncle Sam
people.blurb: 'I Want YOU.' The pointing patriotic mascot of the whole United States. The OG recruiter.

people.name: Audie Murphy
people.blurb: Most decorated U.S. soldier of WWII, then played himself in the movie. Real-life action hero.

people.name: Chesty Puller
people.blurb: Most decorated Marine ever. Marines still say 'Good night, Chesty' before bed. Yes, really.

secret.reveal: Good eye. That's 250 legends + 2 reserved seats — one for Canada 🍁 and one for Greenland 🧊. Statehood pending. You didn't hear it from us.
